Suppose $D(z) = (d_{i,j}(z) )_{i,j=1}^s$ is an $s\times s$ matrix whose elements $d_{i,j}(z)$ are rational functions of a complex variable $z$.

issues.failure_explanation: For non-bushy trees of size p_SL+1, which exist whenever p_SL≥2, ψ(τ;Z,t) sandwiches g^{(ℓ;k)}(y(t)) between functions of Z. It is therefore not a rational function of Z, and sup over scalar z∈C^- of |F| does not bound ‖F(τ;Z,t)‖. The pole cancellation at z=0 is a scalar argument. In the matrix setting, (I−R(Z))^{-1}ψ involves terms like Z^{-1}g'Z, which are unbounded for non-commuting g' and ill-conditioned Z. (I−R(Z))^{-1} does not even exist when J is singular, e.g. the autonomized system with J=diag(J̃,0). Hence Eq:EstimateXi is unproved.
